title: “The Whole Sky All Diamonds” is playing at Loft Story in Brooklyn now...
transcript: This show described itself as the office meets Sleep No more. It's a new immersive play where you step into the role of a new hire at a tech company called füfl. When you arrive, you are free to explore the office a little bit. You can grab a snack at the snack bar, answer the füestion of the day, and even snoop through the boss's computer and phone. If you can guess the password, it's just one, two, three, four, five, six. It's not very secure. They also ask you to decorate your name tag using only pictures, not words. So I drew my cat, Sara. And you can begin to meet some of the characters that you're going to be following over the course of the next hour and a half. Then it's time for the show to start. You begin with a brief orientation, since it's your first day, after all, where they walk you through the space and all of the locations that you're able to explore, and then they let you loose and you can follow whichever character you want. There's only six characters to follow, so in all likelihood, you'll have some interaction with all of them at some point. And the space itself is not that big, only taking up about one floor of a building. But still, I love shows that offer this kind of freedom and the sense that you could come back and see a completely different show. Now, the Show itself is primarily a comedy, but it is also loosely based on Checkov. Now, if you've never seen a Checkov play, I don't think it's going to dampen your enjoyment of the play at all. Just know that everyone's miserable and depressed, there is a ton of unrequited love, and it's probably not gonna be a super happy ending. It all goes to highlight just how soul sucking these types of jobs can be, even though on the surface it seems like such a cool place to work. There's a bar with free snacks, there's nap pods, the C. E. O. Wears Birkenstocks and rides around on a scooter. But behind all of that is a culture that works you to the bone and exploits your labour until you have nothing left to give. So if you are at all into immersive theatre, I would say definitely check this one out. But beware it is only running through August 22nd so you don't have a ton of time.
